meta.title: Heaven on Earth:
meta.titleHighlight: A Heart and Mind Set Above
meta.footer: Bible Study — October 13  ·  Ordinary Glory: Heaven on Earth  ·  Scripture from the NIV

summary.speaker: Leroy Barber
summary.bigIdea: A heart and mind set on heaven gives us strength for hard times and shows us how to bring a little of heaven to earth.
summary.overview: Leroy Barber remembers older church members who sang about heaven to get through hard times, and he says he now understands why. He explains what it means to set our hearts and minds above, and then asks what we should do with that hope.

points.title: A Mind Set on Heaven
points.text: Paul asks us to set our hearts first, then our minds, on things above. When we think from heaven down, and not from earth up, we find strength and hope. This does not make us ignore injustice. It makes us refuse to accept it.

points.title: Bring Heaven Down
points.text: Jesus teaches us to pray that God’s will is done on earth as it is in heaven. Barber says we can answer that prayer by dropping a little heaven into each situation, through peace, fairness, and joy.

points.title: Chosen, Holy, and Loved
points.text: We are chosen, made holy, and loved by God, and we did not earn it. From that love come compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. These are the qualities we can bring from heaven to earth.

points.title: Love as the Binder
points.text: Because God has forgiven us fully, we can forgive others. Love holds everything together, like a binder in a cake. When the heat of hardship comes, love keeps us together and makes the church stronger.

summary.takeaway: This week, choose one small way to bring peace, kindness, or forgiveness into a place that needs it.

col3a.text: “Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things. For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with him in glory.”

matt6.text: “This, then, is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.’”

eph2.text: “For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast.”

col3b.text: “Therefore, as God’s chosen people, holy and dearly loved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.”

col3c.text: “Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone. Forgive as the Lord forgave you. And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity.”

rom5.text: “But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

lewis.name: C. S. Lewis
lewis.quote: If you read history you will find that the Christians who did most for the present world were just those who thought most of the next.

tutu.name: Desmond Tutu
tutu.quote: Without forgiveness, there is no future.

mlk.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
mlk.quote: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.

questions.text: When you hear difficult news, what helps you keep a wider, more hopeful view of the situation?
Think of someone who stayed hopeful through hard times. What do you notice about where their hope seems to come from?
If your neighborhood became a little more like heaven this week, what is one thing you would hope to see?
Think of a moment that felt like a small piece of heaven. What made it feel that way?
How might an ordinary day change if you fully believed you are already loved, with nothing to prove?
Which quality do you most appreciate receiving from others: compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, or patience?
Think of someone you admire for how they forgive. What do you think helps a person forgive like that?
Think of a group that grew closer during a hard time. What helped them stay together?

prayer.label: Closing Prayer
prayer.text:
Dear God,

Thank you that our lives are hidden with Christ in you. When the world feels heavy, help us set our hearts and our minds on things above, so that we find strength and hope.

Teach us to pray, “Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven,” and then to act on that prayer. Show us where we can bring a little of heaven into our homes, our work, and our neighborhoods.

Thank you that we are chosen, holy, and loved, not because of anything we have done. Clothe us with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

Help us to forgive as you have forgiven us. Let your love bind us together, so that when hard times come, they make us stronger as one body.

We ask this in the name of Jesus. Amen.
prayer.source: — Based on this week’s study: a mind set on heaven, bringing heaven to earth, being chosen and loved, and love as the binder.
